KEY MESSAGE 1...Previously mentioned front currently remains
just south of the Crystal Coast this morning per the latest
surface analysis with just some scattered low stratus noted
across ENC mainly along and to the north of this front. This 
front should remain to our south to start our day. However, it 
is then forecast to gradually lift N and E later this afternoon
and evening as an incoming shortwave well to the north in the 
Mid-Atlantic tracks ESE'wards and pulls the front northwards. 
As a result, temps remain slightly cooler compared to previous 
days with aforementioned low stratus this morning and 
potentially earlier start of convection muting temps today. 
Given this, no Heat Advisories have been issued today, although 
spots from Lenoir County southward may get close to 105 for an 
hour or two.

Higher confidence in dangerous heat remains on Monday as the 
front lifts north and re-entrenches ENC in a very hot airmass 
with 1000-850 mb thicknesses once again climbing above 1435m and
widespread Tds in the mid to upper 70s. This could nudge max 
heat index values above 110F in many areas. One caveat to the 
current forecast is that compared to earlier this weekend where 
we had higher mixing ratios, lower mixing ratios look to advect
in from the west under zonal mid level flow so we could mix out
slightly more than currently anticipated and therefore have 
slightly lower dewpoints than forecast. Even if this were to 
occur, much of the area looks to get solidly into heat advisory
criteria so still expecting heat headlines just depends on 
which ones at this point. We continue to encourage anyone 
planning on spending time outdoors to stay hydrated and to limit
exposure to the heat, if able.

Another frontal boundary quickly pushes across NC Monday 
evening before stalling along the coast. Like this weekend, SW 
counties will likely remain hot and humid while Albemarle and 
vicinity see some modest relief. A more widespread cooldown, 
however, is on the horizon late week as a stronger cold front 
dives out of Canada and across the eastern CONUS.

KEY MESSAGE 2...Previously mentioned front currently remains
just south of the Crystal Coast this morning per the latest
surface analysis with just some scattered low stratus noted
across ENC mainly along and to the north of this front. This 
front should remain to our south to start our day. However, it 
is then forecast to gradually lift N and E later this afternoon
and evening as an incoming shortwave well to the north in the 
Mid-Atlantic tracks ESE'wards and pulls the front northwards. 
This is forecast to shift more robust convection threat closer 
to VA but still leaving a favorable environment for sea breeze 
activity, as well as some upstream threats once again making 
their way towards the area in the evening. Evolution will be 
heavily driven by mesoscale factors owing to continued higher 
than average forecast uncertainty owing to large spread in CAMs.
Either way there is a marginal risk for a few stronger storms 
across ENC with the strongest storms bringing a threat for 
damaging wind gusts, frequent lightning, and torrential rainfall
to portions of ENC today. 

A cold front then approaches from the north and west on Monday
evening. Out ahead of this front, a warm and moist airmass will
be in place across ENC resulting in 1500-2500 J/kg of MLCAPE 
but little in the way of shear. However, with PWATs remaining at
or above 2" conditions will once again be favorable for a 
stronger storm or two to impact the area bringing a damaging
wind, frequent lightning, and heavy rain threat. There could be
two focuses for thunderstorm activity on Monday. The first will
be the sea breeze which will be pinned near the coast given
W'rly surface flow which could produce an isolated storm or 
two. A slightly better chance for storms comes from the incoming
front Mon evening as storms upstream track E'wards into the 
area in the evening and overnight. 

KEY MESSAGE 3...A brief return to more climo PoPs is forecast 
Tue and Wed with the seabreeze and stalled front offshore being 
the main focus for showers and thunderstorms. However as we get
into the end of the week a second and stronger cold front looks
to sweep E across NC. This will not only likely end our stretch
of hot and humid conditions but it will also bring increased
precipitation chances with strong to severe thunderstorms not
out of the question. Given how far out this is, there are still
several details to hammer out but will be monitoring trends in 
the forecast for any adjustments in timing and strength of this 
front in the coming days.
